content.title: View a newly created submission in the current browser session
content.intent: Prove that after a successful submission, `/my-submissions` shows the submission in the current browser session with the required table columns, `Under Review` status, matching header count, and per-row `Withdraw` control.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: equivalence partitioning + state / flow + CRUD round-trip. I used the representative transition from one successful submission to its first tracking view because the source promises one post-submit listing outcome with fixed columns, status, count alignment, and row action. No covering array was needed because there is no independent multi-input interaction to combine; the risk-judged default strength would be 2 because no money, auth, or data-loss factor applies to this use-case.
